brief.input: Synthetic case: recycled HDPE and nylon offcuts; their proportions are unknown.
brief.variation: The proportions and visible grit change between received portions.
brief.contamination: Grit identity and amount are not measured.
brief.use_case: A proposed walking surface in a wet doorway; no prototype has been made.
brief.targets: Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.
brief.process: A press is available; its type and tooling have not been confirmed.
brief.available_changes: No new materials, equipment or geometry changes are authorized yet.

plan.answer: You can use this variable HDPE/nylon + grit input without new materials or shape changes by keeping portions separate, preparing by inspection only, and comparing the same process side-by-side. Do not start heated pressing until press type, tooling, and safe processing information for this mix are confirmed. Drainage clearing and visible fit can guide design now; wet-slip needs a proper instrumented assessment by a trained operator, not walking on the prototype or hand feel.

material_routes.title: Keep portions separate, test the range
material_routes.change: Preparation and sorting only. No new binder, modifier, or blending across portions.
material_routes.why: Mixing hides whether HDPE/nylon ratio or grit caused a drainage or surface difference. Separate trials use variation as test information.
steps: Keep each received portion separate with its own label.
Do not blend across portions because proportions and visible grit change.
Make trials from single portions using the same method.
Compare results by portion to see the working range.
tradeoffs: Needs storage space for separate portions.
Does not reduce variation, only makes it visible.
material_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by comparing portion-linked trials for water clearing and surface condition.

material_routes.title: Inspect and remove loose grit only
material_routes.change: Inspection and removal of loose surface grit only, if safe manual handling and suitable facilities allow. No new materials, grinding, or heating assumed.
material_routes.why: Loose grit can block drainage and affect the walking surface. Removing only that fraction lowers one unknown without adding a binder.
steps: Visually inspect each portion for loose grit and large contaminants.
Remove only loose surface grit by safe manual means where facilities allow.
Keep removed fraction separate and keep portion identity.
Record what was removed by observation only, no grit amount assumed.
tradeoffs: Grit identity and amount remain unknown.
Handling depends on confirmed safe facilities.
material_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by noting drainage blocking and surface condition before and after for the same portion.

engineering_routes.title: Same-shape, same-process comparison
engineering_routes.change: No geometry or tooling change. Use only the already-intended insert shape and keep press settings and placement the same for each portion-linked trial.
engineering_routes.why: When proportions and grit vary, holding process and placement constant reduces reliance on unknown material properties and turns variation into comparable information.
steps: Link each trial to one received portion only, do not mix portions.
Record press conditions the same way each run without assuming heated, cold, mould or drying capability.
Place each trial the same way in the doorway position.
Observe water poured in a repeatable way and whether it leaves the walking surface.
tradeoffs: Does not fix variation, only reveals if results follow the portion.
Press capability remains unconfirmed, so trials cannot start until confirmed.
Needs a simple written log to be useful.
engineering_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by comparing water-clearing observation across portions made the same way.

engineering_routes.title: Fit, drainage-path and cleaning observation
engineering_routes.change: No geometry change. Change only installation planning, observation method, and cleaning access using existing features.
engineering_routes.why: Drainage and fit can be observed safely before any slip claim is made, and separates installation effects from material variation.
steps: Check fit and whether water has a clear exit path without ponding at edges.
Observe drainage blocking and visible grit release during water clearing.
Plan cleaning of grit/debris with existing access only.
Keep short exposure as observation only, not weather-durability proof.
tradeoffs: Observation does not prove slip resistance or durability.
Cleaning may be limited without design changes.
Ponding may indicate placement issues rather than material failure.
engineering_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by observing drainage blocking, fit, and cleanability without stepping on a wet unknown prototype.

Confirm press type, tooling, drying/extraction, and safe processing information for HDPE/nylon with grit before any heated trial.
Make portion-linked trials the same way and compare water-clearing and fit observations side-by-side.
Arrange a suitable instrumented slip assessment by a trained operator for the product and wet installation; do not walk on the wet prototype as a check.

How will the insert sit in the doorway and where must drained water go?

sources.scope: General floor-slip testing guidance, including instrumented pendulum assessment by a suitably trained operator under relevant surface conditions. It supplies no measured slip value, acceptance target or qualification for the user's recycled material, and no home walking test substitutes for it. Check the current applicable method for the product and installation.

history.content: How can I use this variable input to make the product within my targets? Propose practical material and engineering adjustments.

You can work with this variable HDPE/nylon + grit mix without new materials or geometry yet by keeping portions separate, preparing by inspection only, and testing the same shape in a controlled way. Any binder, drainage-hole change, or new tooling needs explicit permission because your case currently authorizes no new materials, equipment or geometry changes, and press type/tooling is unconfirmed.
Material route: Keep portions separate, test range. Preparation only, no new binder or equipment: keep each received portion separate and do not blend across portions. Proportions and visible grit change between portions, so mixing hides the cause. Separate trials use the variation as information without needing composition measurement. Next check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by comparing trials from different portions made the same way.
Material route: Inspect and separate loose grit. Preparation only, no new materials: visual sort plus removal of loose surface grit, conditional on safe manual handling and suitable facilities. Grit identity and amount are not measured, and grit can affect drainage and slip. Removing only the loose fraction lowers one unknown without adding a binder. Next check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by observing drainage blocking and wet-surface feel before and after preparation for the same portion.
Engineering route: Same-shape controlled trial log. No geometry change: use only the already-intended insert shape and log press conditions the same way each run. This route does not assume heated, cold, mould, drying or extraction capability - press type and tooling remain unconfirmed. When proportions and grit vary, a consistent process and placement reduces reliance on unknown material properties and shows whether results follow the portion. Next check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by placing each portion-linked trial the same way and observing water clearing and wet-foot grip side-by-side.
Engineering route: Conditional lift-out contained insert - needs permission. CONFLICT: this would change geometry/containment and needs new capability, which your case says is not authorized yet. Use as a conditional option only if geometry and containment work are permitted. Containment and a cleanable path separate walking safety from unknown grit and blend variation, but it cannot start without geometry and tooling permission. Next check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by observing whether water leaves the walking surface and whether grit can be cleaned out without dismantling the doorway.
Confirm what is permitted: manual sorting, use of the existing press, and any geometry or tooling change.
Confirm press type, tooling, and safe processing information for HDPE/nylon with grit before any heated trial.
Make portion-linked trials the same way and compare water clearing and wet-slip observation.
Decide a simple pass observation for drainage and wet grip since numerical acceptance limits are not set.

trial.title: Same-shape comparison across two portions
trial.objective: Use same-shape, same-process trials to see if drainage clearing and visible surface condition follow the received portion, without changing geometry, tooling, or process.
trial.comparison: Trial 1 from Portion A vs Trial 2 from Portion B, both made to the already-intended insert shape with identical press conditions and identical doorway placement. Aim to change one variable per comparison: source portion only.
trial.change: Compare two received portions (Portion A vs Portion B) with no change to insert shape, tooling, or placement; portion identity is the only variable.
keep_fixed: Already-intended insert shape and dimensions - no geometry change
Press settings, placement in press, and placement in doorway position
Water-pour volume, pour point, and observation method
No mixing of portions; each trial linked to one portion only
materials: Received Portion A of recycled HDPE/nylon offcuts with grit, as-received, kept separate
Received Portion B of recycled HDPE/nylon offcuts with grit, as-received, kept separate
Existing doorway test position and water for observation only - no new materials

steps.action: Confirm press capability, tooling, and material suitability for this specific HDPE/nylon/grit mix before any pressing; do not start pressing until confirmed. If unconfirmed, do portion sorting, labelling, and doorway fit/drainage-path planning only.
steps.record: Press type, tooling present/absent, suitability decision, and what remains unconfirmed.

steps.action: Label Portion A and Portion B and keep them separate; inspect and note proportions unknown and visible grit differences without measuring composition.
steps.record: Portion IDs, photos/notes of offcut appearance and visible grit per portion.

steps.action: Subject to confirmed suitable press capability only, form one insert from Portion A and one from Portion B using the same already-intended shape and same press conditions.
steps.record: Portion-to-trial link, press conditions used, and any deviation that would void the comparison.

steps.action: Place each trial in the same doorway position in turn and run the same repeatable water pour, observing water leaving the walking surface.
steps.record: Placement notes, pour volume/point, drainage path, pooling locations, and photos per trial.

checks.target: Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.
checks.method: Place trial in same doorway position, pour same volume of water from same height/point, observe whether water leaves the walking surface and where it pools. Record with photos/notes. This is observation only, not a durability or qualification test.
checks.if_outside: If water pools or clears differently by portion, keep process fixed and start a new comparison linked to portion sorting/inspection notes; do not adjust press or shape in this route.

checks.target: Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.
checks.method: Do not use walking, hand feel, or subjective slip feel. Instrumented pendulum assessment by a suitably trained operator under relevant wet conditions is still needed for the product and installation; result and acceptance threshold are not known. Until then record only visible surface condition and drainage fit.
checks.if_outside: If surface finish or grit exposure differs visibly by portion, log it against portion ID and start a new same-process comparison; do not hand-feel, walk on, or tread the wet prototype as a slip check.
